title: Adopt whitenoise-rs arch-refactor: per-account sessions replace the god object
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/78dc0ac6367f959479dea509953a057bf83f10b1d64cbb0307e7f2dd507e5a91.jpg)

## What changed

`whitenoise-rs` is now pinned to the `arch-refactor` branch (sha `eefe3fe9...`). That branch removed `Whitenoise::get_instance()` and split the god object into one `AccountSession` per account.

## Shim layer

`rust/src/api/mod.rs` holds a private `tokio::sync::OnceCell<Arc<Whitenoise>>` populated by `initialize_whitenoise`. Two helpers:

- `wn() -> &'static Whitenoise` for the few global calls that remain (login, all-accounts, app settings).
- `wn_session(&pubkey) -> Arc<AccountSession>` for everything else.

Init goes through `OnceCell::get_or_try_init`, so two concurrent `initialize_whitenoise` calls share one underlying `Whitenoise::ensure_initialized` run.

## Call-site migration

About 95 sites in `rust/src/api/` moved off the deleted facades onto `session.<ops>()`:

- `session.membership().for_group(&gid)` for accept / decline / archive / unarchive / mute / unmute / pin / mark-read / clear-chat.
- `session.groups()` for visible / by-id / members / admins / create / add-members / remove-members / leave / update-data.
- `session.groups().media()` for upload / download / image-path.
- `session.drafts()`, `session.chat_list()`, `session.mute_list()`, `session.social()`, `session.key_packages()`, `session.push()`, `session.settings()`.

`get_chat_summary` now searches both active and archived chat lists so archived chats render correctly (master commit 8135cbe's intent, under the new API).

## Other adjustments

- `MuteListEntry.account_pubkey` is gone upstream; the shim now passes the pubkey through `MuteListEntry::from_entry`.
- `account.relays(...)` and `user.key_package_*(...)` now take `&Arc<SharedServices>`; the shim passes `&whitenoise.shared`.
- `AccountGroup::get` is gone; the shim uses `session.membership().for_group(&gid).get_or_create(None)`.
- The new `subscribe_to_group_state` from master switched from `Whitenoise::get_instance()` to `wn()`.

## Status

Bridge regenerated. `just precommit` is green. The colony of marmots can stop fetching from the one big burrow and head to their own.

---

Built against `whitenoise-rs` arch-refactor sha `eefe3fe927b53c9c890c2ac1bbc19b269fb41382`.

title: fix: preserve chat list state across screen remounts (#483)
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/f3757fc28c0f4949a066f4338316f1d54ce148f70322d769352aa5b94cafb459.png) Closes #483. Returning to the chat list flashed a loading spinner because go_router's `goNamed` disposes `ChatListScreen`, and on pop the `useChatList` hook re-subscribed to the stream with no cached data. So every back-navigation looked like a cold start. Cache the chat-list map (per pubkey + archived) and the blocked-pubkeys set (per pubkey) at module scope so they outlive widget disposal. `isLoading` now gates on whether an initial snapshot was ever received, not on the current stream's connection state. A remount renders the cached marmots immediately and updates lazily as new stream events arrive. Regression test in `test/hooks/use_chat_list_test.dart` reproduces the bug (fails on old code, passes on the fix). Screen-level test in `test/screens/chat_list_screen_test.dart` locks in the user-flow behavior. Test-side cache reset is wired into `MockWnApi.reset()` so individual test files keep their existing setUp. `just precommit` passes. Coverage 99.36%. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Chat list preserves cached chats when returning from a conversation, eliminating spinner flicker and unnecessary loading. * Blocked-contacts and chat-list caching prevent redundant fetches, improving navigation speed and reducing data usage. * **Tests** * Added/updated tests to cover cached chat behavior and remount scenarios; test teardown now clears related cached state. title: fix: load chat summary via point query so archived chats render correctly
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/5815cb9d270870cfe44a5a5ea958e91422a633c7c2050e363739950f90d4b994.jpg) ## What this fixes Two archive-related bugs share one root cause: - #650: chat header shows "Unknown User" when the chat is archived - #651: the "this user is blocked" banner is missing in archived chats ## Root cause `get_chat_summary` looked up a single chat by calling `whitenoise.get_chat_list(&account).find(...)`. The upstream `get_chat_list()` filters archived chats out, so for any archived chat the lookup returned `ApiError::Other { "Chat not found" }`. Flutter caught the error, `ChatSummary.data` was null, and two render paths broke: - `header.displayName` was null, so the chat header fell back to `unknownUser` - `peerPubkey` was null, which forces `isBlocked = false`, so the blocked banner never showed ## The fix Use the upstream point-query `whitenoise.get_chat_list_item(&account, &group_id)`. It returns the chat regardless of archive state. The upstream docstring at `chat_list.rs:279-316` documents this distinction between list and point queries. One file, three insertions, eight deletions. ## Rebase note You will need to rebase this PR once #649 merges (or I'll just rebase that if this merges first). ## Verification Reporter repro from #651: 1. Block a user 2. Archive that chat 3. Open the chat from the archive list 4. Blocked banner appears 5. Chat header shows the contact's name Fixes #650 Fixes #651 --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance Improvements** * Optimized chat summary retrieval for faster chat data access. title: Dismiss chat list search on swipe-back instead of closing app
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/3dbf71efd665c3c69001188af6b8d1dd8d18f6a4ae803d11851488397070d5d9.png) On Android (e.g. GrapheneOS), the swipe-back gesture used to evict the entire app even when the chat list search bar was open. Wrong target: back should dismiss in-screen state first. The fix wraps `ChatListScreen` in a `PopScope` that intercepts the gesture whenever the search header is revealed or the query field has text. On intercept it unfocuses the keyboard, clears the query, and collapses the header. Once search is no longer visible, back falls through to its normal route pop. To enable parent-driven dismissal, `WnChatList` now accepts an optional `headerOpenNotifier`. When provided, the screen owns the open/closed state and a `useEffect` inside `WnChatList` animates the reveal in response to external changes. Callers without the notifier keep the previous internal state. Tested with three new widget tests covering: header dismissal on back, query clear on back, and pass-through when no search is active. Coverage holds at 99.33%. The marmots wave goodbye to the search bar, not to the whole burrow. Closes #612 --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved back button behavior when search UI is active. Back button now closes the search header instead of exiting the entire screen, then closes the app on subsequent press. * Enhanced header visibility synchronization with improved animation control. * **Tests** * Added comprehensive test coverage for back navigation behavior with active search. * Added tests for header visibility control and scroll position management.

title: fix(android): external signer notification recovery
body: ## Upstream Dependency Resolved: marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#811 has merged, and this PR points at the merged `whitenoise-rs` master revision `49e5f20c43fd72f1d07ea3675350754650955371`. ## Summary - Fix Android background notifications for multi-account external-signer users after reboot / headless foreground-service startup. - Reconcile external signer callbacks from both the UI isolate and foreground-task isolate so every persisted external-signer account has a live callback before notification handling begins. - Register external signer callbacks before ensuring Rust relay subscriptions and before attaching the headless notification stream. - Register app-local Android plugins with the headless foreground-task Flutter engine so the Android signer method channel is available outside `MainActivity`. - Keep headless notification subscriptions from requesting notification permission when no Activity is attached. - Keep the foreground service configured with the `dataSync` service type without restarting an already-running service on every cold start. - Make external signer reconciliation best-effort for non-active accounts while preserving fast-fail behavior for the activating account. ## Review Follow-up - Renamed the lifecycle helper from `ExternalSignerRegistrationService` to `ExternalSignerCallbackRegistry` to make the split from `AndroidSignerService` clearer. - Added Android platform guards in both the callback registry and `AndroidSignerService.registerExternalSigner`. - Removed the short-pubkey logging helper that implied invalid pubkeys were expected. - Removed the `@visibleForTesting` entry point from `NotificationTaskHandler`; tests now exercise retry behavior through task start/repeat/coordination events. - Removed the process-local foreground-service restart flag that would stop/start a running service on every cold start. - Collapsed foreground-task subscription tracking to the subscription source of truth, and clear `NotificationSubscription.isRunning` when the stream closes. - Left the local-account concern as code-is: reconciliation filters `AccountType.external_` before registration, and mixed local/external account tests cover that path. ## Root Cause The boot/reboot foreground task was alive and subscribed to the Rust notification stream, but it did not have external-signer callbacks registered in that headless Dart isolate. Incoming events for Amber-backed accounts could arrive and be persisted, but Rust could not fully process/decrypt them into notification updates until the main app isolate opened and `authProvider` registered the signer callbacks. The desired runtime state is now reconciled in both isolates: every signed-in external-signer account has a registered signer callback in the current process/isolate before notification handling begins. ## Manual Verification Verified on a Pixel 7 Pro with two Amber-backed accounts and a second Android sender device: - Rebooted the Amber device. - Waited for the silent `White Noise connected to relays` foreground notification. - Sent messages to both Amber-backed accounts before opening White Noise. - Both Android notifications appeared while the app remained unopened. - Logs showed the expected order: system foreground task start, external signer callback registration for both accounts, Rust relay subscription ensure, notification stream subscription, received notification updates, displayed notifications. ## Testing - `flutter test --reporter compact test/services/android_signer_service_test.dart test/services/external_signer_callback_registry_test.dart test/services/foreground_service_test.dart test/providers/auth_provider_test.dart` - `just test-flutter-quiet` - `just precommit` - Earlier Android validation: `just when-apk` plus install/manual reboot testing on physical devices. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit ## Release Notes * **New Features** * External signer callback registration is now automatically triggered when the app resumes. * **Improvements** * Enhanced external signer account reconciliation across login, logout, and profile-switching flows. * Notification permission requests are now optional and configurable. * Improved Android foreground service lifecycle handling and coordination. * **Tests** * Expanded test coverage for external signer registration, app lifecycle, and notification handling.

package:build_runner v2.14.1

  • Bug fix: fix crash if a package used to belong to a workspace but was removed from the workspace leaving a stale workspace.ref file.
  • Bug fix: the watch command now always does one build before exiting due to a request from another build_runner process. Fix crashes related to request before build start.

package:build_runner v2.14.0

  • Performance: further improvements to management of files for analysis for 2x faster incremental builds.
  • Performance: default to AOT compilation for commands other than run. This costs more initial startup time but gives faster builds afterwards. Fall back to JIT if the compile fails due to use of dart:mirrors. Use the --force-jit flag if you want the old default JIT builder compile. Use the --force-aot flag to turn off the fallback to JIT compile.
  • Add support for asset: scheme to the --build-filter flag. It is like package: but for the whole package, not just lib. For example, package:a/b.dart is the same as asset:a/lib/b.dart.
  • Paths specified using --build-filter when using the --workspace flag now apply to the current package, not the workspace root. Other packages must be referred to using package: or asset: schemes.
  • Add OSC 8 hyperlinks for logged input paths.
  • Better handling of deletions of files during the build: if the file is not needed ignore the deletion, if it's needed try to use the cached version, as a last resort restart the build.
  • Defer deletions of files by build_runner until the build is complete. Don't write files unless the contents changed. These reduce unnecessary work by tools that watch the filesystem.
  • --workspace flag is no longer experimental, remove the warning.
  • Add --workspace flag to clean command, use it to clear the cache used for a --workspace build.
  • Add new command stop: run dart run build_runner stop to terminate a running watch or serve command in the current package or workspace. If a build is in progress, the build will complete first.
  • Add locking: build_runner will wait for any already-running command before running. If there is an already-running watch or serve command, it will be closed after the currently-running build, as if you ran the new dart run build_runner stop.
  • Note: the daemon command ignores build_runner stop and ignores the new locking as it uses its own locking.
  • Bug fix: small correctness fix in input tracking.
  • Bug fix: fix corner case that caused missing outputs with build_runner serve when directories were specified with a port, for example build_runner serve web:0. Before the fix, non-optional outputs to cache under web would be skipped unless they were used by another build step. With the fix, all non-optional outputs under web are built and served.
  • Bug fix: when building with --workspace generate the entrypoint and compiled artifacts under the workspace root instead of the current package root.

title: fix(android): enable boot auto-restart for foreground service
body:
## Summary

Restore notification delivery after device reboot and after app updates. The original fix (re-enable the plugin's boot/package-replaced receivers + set the Dart auto-run flags) turned out to be necessary but not sufficient — the foreground service restarted post-reboot but ran an empty task handler, so messages still didn't surface as notifications until the user reopened the app. This PR closes that loop:

- **Boot/upgrade auto-restart**: re-enabled the plugin's `RebootReceiver` / `RestartReceiver` and set `autoRunOnBoot: true` + `autoRunOnMyPackageReplaced: true`.
- **Process-scoped JNI context**: new `WhitenoiseApplication` runs `Keyring.initializeNdkContext()` in `Application.onCreate`, so Rust has the Android Context regardless of which component (Activity / Service / Receiver) starts the process.
- **Headless work in the task isolate**: extracted `NotificationSubscription` from `notificationListenerProvider` so it can run independent of the widget tree. New `_NotificationTaskHandler` bootstraps Rust + reads locale from persisted state, and on `starter=system` (boot/package-replaced) starts its own subscription.
- **Cross-isolate coordination**: main isolate sends `main_started` / `main_stopped` via `FlutterForegroundTask.sendDataToTask` so exactly one isolate owns the notification channel at a time.
- **Pending-tap handoff**: a notification fired from the task isolate persists its payload via `FlutterForegroundTask.saveData`; the main isolate consumes it on launch / resume and routes to the right chat (switching the active account first if needed).

Fixes #488.

## Why

Currently, after a device reboot the foreground service does not auto-restart, so notifications silently stop working until the user opens the app. Two stacked misconfigurations caused this:

**1. Receivers were disabled in the manifest.** [c3b4a1909](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/commit/c3b4a1909) added `android:enabled="false"` + `tools:node="replace"` as defense-in-depth against an upgrade-path crash. The *actual* root cause of that crash — `foregroundServiceType 0x201` persisted in native `SharedPreferences` while the manifest declared only `dataSync` — was already mitigated by the one-time prefs cleanup in `MainActivity.onCreate()`. That cleanup has been shipped since 2026-02-19, so any active user has run it.

**2. The Dart-side flags were never set.** `ForegroundTaskOptions.autoRunOnBoot` defaults to `false`. The plugin's `RebootReceiver.onReceive` reads this from persisted options and early-returns unless it's `true` — so even if the manifest disable were removed, boot restart still wouldn't happen.

Both fixes are required. The receiver is the plugin's *only* boot-restart mechanism, and it only fires when the Dart flags opt in.

## GrapheneOS impact

This is particularly important for GrapheneOS users. They typically don't run sandboxed Google Play Services, so the MIP05 FCM-based push plan won't reach them — the foreground service is their only notification path. Without boot auto-restart, every reboot silently breaks notifications until the app is manually reopened.

The receivers use pure AOSP APIs (`BOOT_COMPLETED`, `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED`, `AlarmManager`) with no GMS dependency, so they work on GrapheneOS.

## Known limitation: first install / upgrade

`autoRunOnBoot` and `autoRunOnMyPackageReplaced` are persisted by the plugin only when Dart calls `FlutterForegroundTask.init()`. On the very first install or upgrade to a build containing this PR, the previous Dart-persisted flag values are still in `SharedPreferences` (default `false`), so:

- The `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED` broadcast that fires immediately after the upgrade reads the stale `false` and skips auto-start.
- A reboot before the user has opened the new build will likewise skip auto-start.

After the user opens the app one time on this build, the new flags are persisted and every subsequent reboot or update auto-starts correctly.

A native-side workaround (seeding the plugin's `SharedPreferences` from `WhitenoiseApplication.onCreate`) would close this one-time gap, but it couples our code to plugin-internal pref schema — the same layer that produced the `0x201` bitmask incident in [c3b4a1909](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/commit/c3b4a1909). Deferring with documentation is the safer trade for a one-time UX hiccup.

## Residual risk

A user who hasn't launched the app since before 2026-02-19 could still have stale `0x201` in their prefs. On next reboot, `RebootReceiver` would try to start the service with that stale type and crash. Likelihood is low (2+ months of launches since the cleanup shipped), but non-zero. The `MainActivity.onCreate()` cleanup stays in place as a safety net on the next normal launch.

## Android 15 note

If `targetSdk` is ever bumped to 35+, the OS itself blocks boot-launched `dataSync` foreground services regardless of plugin setup. At that point the service type needs to change (likely to `remoteMessaging` or `specialUse`). Not blocking today; worth flagging for when the SDK bump happens.

## Test plan

- [x] `just precommit` passes (formatting, linting, Flutter + Rust tests, 99.36% coverage)
- [x] Spike confirmed on a real device that the task isolate can reach Rust, platform channels, and persisted accounts on a freshly rebooted process (`starter=system` path)
- [x] Spike confirmed `flutter_local_notifications` can fire from the task isolate
- [ ] Manual: install on a Pixel, send a test message, reboot, confirm a notification appears without opening the app
- [ ] Manual: repeat on GrapheneOS (no sandboxed Play Services)
- [ ] Manual: verify the in-app/background handoff doesn't produce duplicate notifications when toggling between foreground and background while messages arrive

title: Add disappearing messages support
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/0074236e7be0ccf1467235e0f709fda9c31f977d1295cb471ea3a9540e8a17cc.jpg)

Needs: marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#730

Implements the Flutter side of disappearing messages. When an admin sets a TTL on a group, every new message stored gets an expires_at timestamp. A background task in the Rust layer sweeps expired rows every 30 seconds and notifies the UI.

## What changed

**Rust API layer** (rust/src/api/): Added expires_at field to ChatMessage, two new functions (set_disappearing_messages, get_disappearing_message_duration), bumped whitenoise-rs and mdk-core dependencies to pick up the disappearing messages support.

**Hook** (lib/hooks/use_disappearing_messages.dart): Manages loading and setting the disappearing message duration per group. Exposes current duration, loading/saving states, and error handling.

**Group info screen**: Admins see a dropdown selector (Off / 30s / 5min / 1hr / 1day / 1week) to configure the disappearing message timer for the group.

**Message bubbles**: Messages with an expiration timestamp display a small timer icon next to the timestamp, so users know the message will disappear.

**L10n**: Added 12 new localization keys across all 8 locale files.

**Tests**: 58 new tests covering the format utility (24), the hook (19), the bubble ephemeral indicator (7), and the group info screen dropdown (8). All 4009 Flutter tests and 42 Rust tests pass. Precommit green.

## Design decisions

- **Dedicated API functions over FlutterGroupDataUpdate**: flutter_rust_bridge doesn't support Option<Option<T>>, so set/get disappearing messages use standalone functions, which gives a cleaner separation of concerns.
- **No retroactive expiry**: Changing the duration only affects new messages, matching the Rust layer's approach and Signal/WhatsApp behavior.
- **Timer icon, not countdown**: The bubble shows a static timer icon to indicate the message is ephemeral, while the Rust layer handles actual cleanup on its 30-second sweep cycle.

This marmot built hourglasses into the message bubbles. When your time is up, poof.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Group disappearing messages: admins can pick preset durations (seconds→weeks) or turn Off; updates show success/error notices.

* **Localization**
  * Added localized strings and pluralized duration formats across languages; duration labels are human-friendly and preview expirations.

* **UI**
  * Group settings include a duration selector; messages with expirations show an ephemeral timer indicator and are removed when expired.

* **Tests**
  * New tests covering setting flows, duration formatting, ephemeral UI, and expiration handling.

title: Search 2.0: cross-group message content search in chat list
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/47de183d5336f22041f5c8fca61984de8172d4dcf5ac85667093f003d3bcd185.jpg)

This marmot dug through every burrow to find your messages.

## What changed

Chat list search now finds chats by message content, not just chat names. Type a query in the home screen search bar and chats containing matching messages appear in the results with the matched message shown as the subtitle.

## How it works

1. User types in the search bar
2. Name-matched chats appear instantly (synchronous client-side filter, same as before)
3. After a 300ms debounce, `searchMessages` fires a single SQL query across all groups via the Rust API
4. Chats with matching messages merge into the list, showing the matched snippet as subtitle

The search runs through whitenoise-rs `search_messages(pubkey, query, limit)` (commit 8605c2c), which queries `aggregated_messages` joined against `accounts_groups` to scope results to the user's chats. Position is computed per-group via `PARTITION BY mls_group_id` so the frontend can still jump to the right page within each conversation.

## Changes

**Rust layer**
- Bumped whitenoise-rs to 8605c2c (adds cross-group `search_messages`)
- Added `mls_group_id` to `SearchResult` struct (upstream breaking change)
- Added `search_messages` API function wrapping `whitenoise.search_messages`
- Updated `fetch_aggregated_messages_for_group` for new `PaginationOptions` struct

**Flutter layer**
- New `useChatListSearch` hook: debounced cross-group message search, returns `{messageSnippets, matchedGroupIds, isSearching}`
- New `filterChatsBySearchWithMessageMatches` function: merges name and message-content matches
- `ChatListTile` accepts optional `searchSnippet` that overrides the subtitle during search
- `ChatListScreen` wires the hook, new filter, snippets, and loading indicator
- `WnSearchAndFilters` passes `isLoading` through to the search field

**Tests**
- 10 new hook tests (debounce, cancellation, grouping, error handling)
- 6 new filter function tests
- Fixed pre-existing `SearchResult` compilation in 3 test files (missing `mlsGroupId`)

Closes #350

body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/0efb557cc20f0285c0177e57413ee19c64fca101aeeb4e59ec45ffa01edefef3.png)

> **⚠️ DO NOT MERGE — this PR is a work-in-progress checkpoint, not a finished feature.**
>
> It's here for visibility and review feedback, not for merging into master.

---

## What this is

A battery profiling system for staging builds. The goal: find out exactly where CPU time goes so we can stop guessing about battery drain and start measuring it.

### The pieces

**Dart-side tracer** (`lib/profiling/tracer.dart`)
- Ring buffer (10k spans) with `Tracer.begin()` / `Span.end()` API
- Zero production footprint via `tracer_stub.dart` — compiler eliminates dead code entirely
- Perfetto JSON export for visualization at [ui.perfetto.dev](https://ui.perfetto.dev)

**Rust span integration** (`lib/providers/rust_log_listener_provider.dart`)
- Parses perf spans from Rust log stream via `_maybeInjectPerfSpan`
- Injects them into the shared ring buffer with separate tids for parallel flamegraph lanes
- Also available via `flushRustSpans()` FFI for direct drain

**Span statistics engine** (`lib/profiling/span_stats.dart`)
- Groups spans by name, computes total/avg/p50/p95/p99 per operation
- Histogram generation for distribution visualization
- Ranks operations by cumulative CPU time — hottest path first

**Profiling screen** (`lib/screens/profiling_screen.dart`)
- Live stats table refreshing every second
- Layer filtering (Dart vs Rust spans), sorting, threshold controls
- Snapshot comparison for before/after measurements
- One-tap Perfetto trace export via share sheet

**Instrumented sites** — nine priority hooks and services now emit spans:
- `use_chat_list` — stream subscription lifecycle
- `use_chat_messages` — message stream + decryption
- `use_chat_profile` — profile metadata fetches
- `use_chat_scroll` — scroll event processing
- `use_mark_as_read` — read receipt FFI calls
- `use_user_search` — search + the 5-second `accountFollows` tick
- `notification_provider` — notification stream processing
- `message_service` — message send hot path
- `user_service` — metadata fetch chains

### What's missing before this could merge

- [ ] Tests need updating to account for instrumented code paths
- [ ] Coverage verification (`just coverage`)
- [ ] Precommit pass (`just precommit`)
- [ ] Review of conditional import guard under all build flavors

---

*A marmot that can't measure its tunnels is just digging in the dark.* 🦫📊

body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/4738ba181d5753cb3032b8ad79818dd95eb1f583be0d4d51c17affe3060b7060.png) Fixes #505. Adds a non-blocking update prompt for Android users when a newer White Noise build is available on Zapstore. **How it works** On app start, the app queries `relay.zapstore.dev` for the kind-32267 software application event for `org.parres.whitenoise`. The `a` tag on that event points at the latest kind-30063 release artifact set, which encodes the version as `org.parres.whitenoise@`. That version string is compared against the installed version (via `PackageInfo`). If Zapstore has something newer, a dismissible info banner appears at the top of the chat list screen with an "Update now" button that opens the Zapstore listing. **What's in this PR** - `rust/src/api/zapstore.rs`: new Rust API function `fetch_latest_zapstore_version()` using `nostr-sdk` to query the Zapstore relay (10s timeout, short-lived connection) - `lib/hooks/use_zapstore_update.dart`: Flutter hook that calls the Rust function, compares CalVer versions numerically, and returns `(availableVersion, isDismissed, dismiss)` - `lib/screens/chat_list_screen.dart`: update banner wired in; takes priority over the welcome notice; falls back to `platformDefault` launch if `externalApplication` fails - l10n strings for all 8 supported languages (de, en, es, fr, it, pt, ru, tr) - `url_launcher` added as a dependency - Tests: 12 hook tests, 7 screen-level tests, 3 Rust unit tests **Note for reviewers** Design will need to be improved by @josefinalliende or @untreu2, this is just the basic implementation to make sure the rust side of the code is implemented in the flutter side :slightly_smiling_face:. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * In-app update banner that notifies when a newer Zapstore version is available (shows version), dismissible, prioritized over welcome notices, and opens Zapstore with a fallback launch flow. * Developer settings toggle to simulate the update banner for testing. * **Localization** * Added translations for the update banner in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, and Turkish. * **Tests** * Added unit and widget tests for the update flow, version comparisons, URL launch fallback, dismissal, and simulation.
